Adjoint of an event to first and second order, with the transpose of the Heun transport
[Events (2)](methods-events.html#eq-fixed-heun). [Notation](methods-overview.html#notation);
arguments `events` and `derivMode = "reverse"` or `"forward-reverse"` of
[`cppODE()`](../reference/cppODE.html), `cotangent` of [`solveODE()`](../reference/solveODE.html).
Derivatives are in $\theta = (x_0, p)$; event times $t_e$ and root functions $h_e$ depend on
$\theta$ through $p$.

## Adjoint of an event {#event-adjoint}

An event is a separate map between two steps. The
[Heun transport](methods-events.html#time-triggered-events) shifts to the event surface, resets,
and shifts back to the grid time, each shift over the firing-time residual $\delta t^{*}$, zero in
value with nonzero derivatives. It reduces to the saltation relation
[]{#eq-saltation}
$$
  \mathrm{d}x^{+} = R'\!\left(\mathrm{d}x^{-} + f^{-}\, \delta t^{*}\right)
              - f^{+}\, \delta t^{*}, \tag{1}
$$
with $R$ the resets and $R'$ their Jacobian. For a root event $h_e(x, t, p) = 0$,
$\delta t^{*} = -(\nabla_x h_e \cdot \mathrm{d}x + \partial h_e/\partial p \cdot \mathrm{d}p) / \dot h_e$
by the implicit function theorem; for a time-triggered event at $t^{*} = t_e(p)$,
$\delta t^{*} = (\partial t_e/\partial p)\cdot \mathrm{d}p$.

Contracted with the cotangent $\lambda^{+}$ after the jump, the $\delta t^{*}$ terms of the linear
map [(1)](#eq-saltation) collect into one scalar $\eta$,
[]{#eq-saltation-adjoint}
$$
  \eta = \left(\lambda^{+}\right)^{\mathsf T}
           \left(R' f^{-} - f^{+}\right),
  \qquad
  \lambda^{-}
    = R'^{\mathsf T}\lambda^{+}
    + \eta \left(\frac{\partial\, \delta t^{*}}{\partial x}\right)^{\!\mathsf T}, \tag{2}
$$
and the parameter cotangent gains $\eta\,(\partial\, \delta t^{*}/\partial p)^{\mathsf T}$:

| event | state gains | parameters gain |
|:--|:--|:--|
| root | $-(\eta/\dot h_e)\nabla_x h_e$ | $-(\eta/\dot h_e)\,\partial h_e/\partial p$ |
| time-triggered | nothing | $\eta\,\partial t_e/\partial p$ |

$R'^{\mathsf T}$ is applied reset by reset, in reverse order: a replacement removes the component
cotangent, an addition keeps it, a multiplication by $v$ scales it by $v$, plus the derivatives of
a state- or parameter-dependent $v$. The adjoint of a jump needs $f$ at both ends, $\nabla_x h_e$,
$\dot h_e$ and the derivatives of reset and event-time expressions; no Jacobian of $f$, since every
shift term has the residual as a factor.

Multistep methods restart after a jump from $z_0 = x$, $z_1 = h\, f(x, t)$, other slots zero, $h$
the first step size, so the history cotangent $\bar z_j$ collapses onto $x$:
[]{#eq-restart-collapse}
$$
  \bar x = \bar z_0 + h\, J^{\mathsf T} \bar z_1,
  \qquad
  \bar p = h \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial p}\right)^{\!\mathsf T} \bar z_1, \tag{3}
$$
and higher slots nothing, as at the start of the trajectory.

## Second order at an event {#event-second-order}

$\delta t^{*}$ is zero in value with a nonzero first derivative, so
[]{#eq-dt-squared}
$$
  (\delta t^{*})^{2} = 0, \qquad
  \mathrm{d}(\delta t^{*})^{2} = 2\, \delta t^{*}\,\mathrm{d}\,\delta t^{*} = 0,
  \qquad
  \mathrm{d}^{2}(\delta t^{*})^{2} = 2\,(\mathrm{d}\,\delta t^{*})^{2} \neq 0 , \tag{4}
$$
so terms of order $(\delta t^{*})^{2}$ drop from the gradient but not from the Hessian. Three such
terms enter a jump, for time-triggered events ($\delta t^{*} = t_e - \mathrm{scalar}(t_e)$) as for
root events: both use the same transport, transposed as a reversed program. If the jump height
moves with a parameter, [(1)](#eq-saltation) alone is exact in value but wrong in the tangents: the
backward shift
$\bar x^{*}_{+} = \bigl(I - \delta t^{*}\, J(x^{*}_{+})\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\bar x^{+}$
multiplies $\delta t^{*}$ by a factor nonzero in value.

**Curvature of the shift.** Each half of the transport is a Heun step,
[]{#eq-heun-curvature}
$$
  x^{*} = x^{-} + f^{-}\, \delta t^{*}
           + \tfrac{1}{2}\, \kappa^{-}\, (\delta t^{*})^{2},
  \qquad
  \kappa = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} f + \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}, \tag{5}
$$
with $\kappa\,\delta t^{*}$ the difference of the two right-hand sides the step evaluates, so no
Jacobian.

**Post-jump state.** The checkpoint keeps only $x^{-}$. A reconstruction of $x^{+}$ by the bare
reset would give $\partial x^{+} / \partial t^{*} = 0$, whereas
[]{#eq-post-jump-motion}
$$
  \frac{\partial x^{+}}{\partial t^{*}}
    = f^{-} - f^{+} , \tag{6}
$$
so the reconstruction runs the transport, not the reset.

**Quadrature.** The parameter cotangent
[]{#eq-quadrature-split}
$$
  \bar p_{k} = \int_{t_0}^{T} q_{k}\,\mathrm{d}t
             = \int_{t_0}^{t^{*}} q_{k}\,\mathrm{d}t
             + \int_{t^{*}}^{T} q_{k}\,\mathrm{d}t,
  \qquad
  q_{k} = \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial p_{k}}\right)^{\!\mathsf T}\!\lambda, \tag{7}
$$
is split at $t^{*}$, where $q_{k}$ jumps; the moving split point contributes
[]{#eq-quadrature-jump}
$$
  \frac{\partial \bar p_{k}}{\partial \theta}
  \;\supset\;
  \Big( q_{k}(t^{*-}) - q_{k}(t^{*+}) \Big)\,
  \frac{\partial t^{*}}{\partial \theta} . \tag{8}
$$
Only parameters whose $\partial f / \partial p_{k}$ depends on a reset state contribute.

All three are scaled by the residual, zero in value with tangent
$\partial t^{*} / \partial \theta$, and leave the gradient unchanged. The root-event residual is
[]{#eq-root-residual}
$$
  \delta t^{*} = -\,\frac{h_e - \mathrm{scalar}(h_e)}{\dot h_e},
  \qquad
  \dot h_e = \frac{\partial h_e}{\partial t} + \nabla_x h_e \cdot f , \tag{9}
$$
read at the checkpointed state, which holds $\partial x / \partial \theta$ at a fixed time since
localization ignores tangents; $\nabla_x h_e$ contracts it to the firing time.

## Transpose of the root transport {#root-sandwich}

With the names of [Events (2)](methods-events.html#eq-fixed-heun), the jump is the composition
[]{#eq-root-sandwich}
$$
\begin{aligned}
  x_{E} &= x^{-} + f_{1}\, \delta t^{*}, &
  x^{*} &= x^{-} + \tfrac{1}{2}(f_{1} + f_{2})\, \delta t^{*}, &
  x^{*}_{+} &= R(x^{*}, t^{*}), \\
  x_{B} &= x^{*}_{+} - \tilde f_{1}\, \delta t^{*}, &
  x^{+} &= x^{*}_{+} - \tfrac{1}{2}(\tilde f_{1} + \tilde f_{2})\, \delta t^{*}, &
\end{aligned} \tag{10}
$$
with $f_{2} = f(x_{E}, t^{*})$, $\tilde f_{1} = f(x^{*}_{+}, t^{*})$ and $f_{1}$, $\tilde f_{2}$ at
the grid time $t_*^{(0)}$. The program is transposed assignment by assignment. A closed form
pruned by order in $\delta t^{*}$ is valid for the gradient but, by [(4)](#eq-dt-squared), not for
the Hessian.

Every assignment containing the residual contributes to it, two through the $\theta$-dependent
$t^{*}$ in $f_{2}$ and $\tilde f_{1}$:
[]{#eq-shift-clock}
$$
  \overline{\delta t^{*}} \;\supset\;
    \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}\right)_{\!(x^{*}_{+}, t^{*})}\!\!\cdot \bar{\tilde f}_{1}
    + \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}\right)_{\!(x_{E}, t^{*})}\!\!\cdot \bar f_{2} . \tag{11}
$$
Both cotangents have a factor $\delta t^{*}$: [(11)](#eq-shift-clock) is absent from the gradient,
at full strength in the Hessian, zero for autonomous $f$, and missing from a pruned form.

The forward correction $-\tfrac{1}{2}(\ddot h_e / \dot h_e)\,(\delta t^{*})^{2}$ of the residual,
[Events (6)](methods-events.html#eq-dt-star-second), has the chain factor
$1 + 2 c_{2}\, \delta t^{*}$, $c_{2} = -\ddot h_e / (2\dot h_e)$, one in value with a second-order
tangent; the transpose applies it to $\partial\, \delta t^{*} / \partial x$.

The sweep binds the tangent storage of every buffer it passes to a generated contraction
([forward over reverse](methods-forward-reverse.html)). Jump-transpose reads of such a buffer are
multiplied by $\delta t^{*}$, so an unbound buffer leaves value and gradient correct and the Hessian
wrong by a rank-one term.

**Derivative of the residual.** Since $\dot h_e$ depends on the state,
[]{#eq-root-quotient}
$$
  \frac{\partial\, \delta t^{*}}{\partial x}
    = -\frac{\nabla_x h_e}{\dot h_e}
      - \frac{\delta t^{*}}{\dot h_e}\, \nabla_x \dot h_e ,
  \qquad
  \nabla_x \dot h_e = \nabla_x \frac{\partial h_e}{\partial t}
                + \left(\nabla_x^{2} h_e\right) f + J^{\mathsf T}\nabla_x h_e , \tag{12}
$$
with the second term absent from the gradient and at full strength in the Hessian. The generator
differentiates $\dot h_e$ as one expression, so all three terms of $\nabla_x \dot h_e$ are
present, also those vanishing for a time-independent $h_e$ linear in the state; in $\theta$ it
gives $\partial^{2} h_e/\partial\theta\,\partial t$,
$(\partial \nabla_x h_e/\partial\theta)\cdot f$ and
$(\partial f/\partial\theta)^{\mathsf T}\nabla_x h_e$. A forcing in $h_e$ is differentiated in $t$
through a rate leaf on the expression graph, printed as the derivative of the PCHIP interpolant.

**Time-dependent resets.** A reset value $v$ with explicit time dependence is applied at $t^{*}$:
[]{#eq-reset-clock}
$$
  \frac{\partial x^{*}_{+}}{\partial t^{*}} \;\supset\; c\,
  \frac{\partial v}{\partial t}, \qquad
  c = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{add,} \\ 1 & \text{replace,} \\ x^{*}_{k} &
  \text{multiply,}\end{cases} \tag{13}
$$
with $k$ the reset component, a first-order contribution to $\eta$ of
[(2)](#eq-saltation-adjoint): without it the gradient is wrong. The transposed reset therefore
receives $t^{*}$ as a dual, so $\partial v/\partial\theta$ includes $\partial t^{*}/\partial\theta$.
Such a value evaluates $t^{*}$ directly and is accurate to the root tolerance, not the integration tolerance; for a value
depending only on the state at $t^{*}$, the smooth trajectory damps the localization error.

With $R = \mathrm{id}$, [(10)](#eq-root-sandwich) is the identity and the transpose cancels term by
term. Tests compare the transpose with a nested-dual evaluation of the transport, and the second
order over a trajectory with forward over forward on the same steps.

## Moving event rows

If $t^{*}$ depends on a parameter, the row at the firing time moves with it. A functional
$w^{\mathsf T} x$ seeded on that row compares states at different times for different parameters
and has no derivative; a cotangent on the requested output times is well posed.
